global.concept_prompt:
Ultra-realistic, cinematic, faceless short-form video that takes the viewer on a single continuous first-person journey: a panicked sprint to and through the door of a modest, mysterious structure in a dramatic remote place, an immediate look down the staircase that descends right inside the door, a continuous POV descent down that staircase, and a calm off-POV reveal of a hidden, secret, luxurious living space concealed below.

The video must be composed for a vertical 9:16 frame and must always remain upright, never sideways or horizontal.

The video ALWAYS follows the same fixed five-beat format — only the setting, the structure, and the hidden interior change between episodes:
1. FIRST-PERSON POV at FULL-TILT SPRINT — the lone traveler runs STRAIGHT AT the structure's entrance DOOR and THROWS THE DOOR OPEN WITH HIS HAND. The video opens already in full-tilt motion: the runner is sprinting flat out across a dramatic remote setting toward the door. K0 must have the DOOR AT 20–25 METRES AHEAD, CENTERED IN THE FRAME as the dominant focal point. The world RUSHES PAST at real sprint speed (~6–7 m/s) — ground flying past beneath, terrain at the frame edges blurring from forward motion. AT THE FINAL MOMENT OF THE CLIP, as he reaches the door at full sprint, his HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame — palm out, fingers extended — and SHOVES the door open INWARD in one fast continuous motion. The hand is VISIBLE making contact with the door; the door does NOT open by itself or automatically — it is the visible hand that pushes it open. The door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under his hand's push, and he continues forward THROUGH the doorway WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE, WITHOUT PAUSING, WITHOUT ANY FRAME OF STILLNESS. The hand contacts the door AT sprint speed — no slowing, no hand-reach-from-distance. By the end of scene 1 (K1) the runner is JUST INSIDE the structure, mid-stride, facing INTO the structure with the STAIRCASE GOING DOWN IMMEDIATELY VISIBLE AHEAD — the structure's interior is essentially a small entrance landing, NOT a room to walk across; the stairs descend right inside the doorway.
2. FIRST-PERSON POV — a brief moment as the runner steps forward to the very top of the staircase, the camera angling DOWNWARD into the descending steps. The staircase has been visible ahead since K1; now the camera arrives at its edge and looks DOWN into it. He is still hurrying. By the end of scene 2 (K2) the camera is AT THE TOP of the straight step staircase, angled DOWN into the descending steps — the staircase dominates the frame, going DOWN into warm light from below.
3. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT down the straight step staircase from top to bottom. The camera stays in POV the entire clip — it NEVER lifts off the head, NEVER cuts to a third-person view, NEVER skips ahead, NEVER teleports, NEVER floats through stairs, NEVER passes through walls. The camera is angled DOWNWARD throughout, watching the steps roll past beneath as he walks down them one by one. Per-step bob: camera dips as each foot lands on the next step down, with a brief settle, then the next step. Warm amber light grows brighter as he descends. THE FOOTSTEPS ON THE STAIRS ARE PROMINENTLY AUDIBLE — each step creates a clear, distinct sound (timber creak / concrete thud / stone tap depending on the staircase material) that DOMINATES the audio of this clip. The pace can ease slightly here — he is reaching safety. By the end of scene 3 (K3) he is at the BOTTOM step or just stepping off it into the lower room.
4. OFF-POV (third-person) FIRST REVEAL of the hidden luxurious interior. The camera switches to off-POV positioned IN THE LOWER ROOM, looking across the room. The traveler — seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/body LOCKED — has just emerged from the staircase and is walking calmly in ONE consistent forward direction across the room, unbothered. The camera slowly TRACKS LATERALLY across the room as he walks. The staircase entrance is a SUBTLE, SECONDARY element at ONE edge of the frame — only the bottom 1–2 steps and the wall opening visible, the higher steps CUT OFF out of frame; the man is IN the lower room, NOT on the staircase. The hidden luxury interior is the dominant feature of the frame.
5. OFF-POV (third-person) HOUSE-TOUR — the traveler walks toward and through an open archway or doorway into ANOTHER luxurious room of the hidden residence — same materials, lighting palette, and continuity as the lower room. The camera follows him from behind in one smooth continuous house-tour move. His clothing, body, silhouette, and gait are IDENTICAL to scene 4.

CAMERA: Scenes 1–3 are real FIRST-PERSON POV — a battered body-cam strapped to the traveler's chest. Scene 1 is EXTREME body-cam shake: NO frame is steady, every frame has motion (dipping, rising, tilting, rotating); water droplets streak the lens (in storm/rain/coastal settings) or motion blur from speed elsewhere; lens splash; irregular sudden jolts (the runner stumbles slightly, recovers); barely-controlled raw amateur footage like a foot pursuit body-cam. Scene 2 is a brief hurried POV with reduced bob (he is no longer sprinting). Scene 3 is the CONTINUOUS POV DESCENT — step-by-step bob down the staircase, never lifts off the head. Scenes 4–5 are calm off-POV third-person — the traveler is seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/appearance LOCKED. The POV-to-off-POV transition happens cleanly between scenes 3 and 4, at the bottom of the descent when the man has stepped off the last step into the lower room.

RUNNING & MOVEMENT MUST LOOK REAL — highest priority and a persistent weakness. In scene 1 the camera must JOLT EXTREMELY DOWN-UP and side-to-side with EACH footfall in a FAST sprint cadence (about 3–4 strides per second — a flat-out sprint, NOT a jog). The frame rotates 8–15 degrees per stride before recentering. Motion blur at frame edges from speed. Panicked panting breath audible. CRUCIAL: NO FRAME IS STEADY — every frame has visible motion; the image is BARELY in control. Add irregular sudden jolts (the runner stumbles slightly mid-stride, almost-trips, recovers — not a perfectly metronomic shake). Water droplets streak the lens in rain/storm/coastal settings; in dry settings substitute lens flare, dust kicked up, or motion blur from speed. Lens splash. The camera looks like a battered amateur body-cam from a foot pursuit. The WORLD MUST RUSH PAST the camera at high speed — the ground FLIES past beneath, terrain at the edges RACES past as a blur from forward motion (the K0→K1 spatial delta of 20–25 metres forces this). Each stride has a real biomechanical SURGE-AND-SETTLE — the camera LURCHES FORWARD as the foot pushes off, briefly floats during airborne phase, then JOLTS DOWN HARD as the next foot lands. The runner's forearms OCCASIONALLY appear at the BOTTOM edge of the frame as he pumps them — brief, natural, NOT exaggerated, NOT the focus. The door REMAINS the dominant focal point for most of the clip with brief 1–2 shoulder-glances backward. NEVER a smooth tracking shot, dolly, gimbal, Steadicam, gliding camera, floating camera, weightless camera, skating motion, 'walking with shake on top', metronomic shake, or steady frame.

DOOR ACTION (scene 1, end) — HAND OPENS IT, FAST: the door must be a real, solid, three-dimensional object with thickness, hinges, and hardware. The door does NOT open by itself or automatically — it is the visible HAND that pushes it open. At the final moment of the clip, as the runner reaches the door at sprint speed, his HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame (palm out, fingers extended) and SHOVES the door open INWARD in one fast continuous motion. The hand contacts the door AT sprint speed — NO slowing, NO hand-reach-from-distance (the hand comes into frame just as the door is being reached, not from far away). The door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under his hand's push, and he continues THROUGH the doorway WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE. The door NEVER opens outward toward the camera, NEVER opens slowly, NEVER opens by itself, NEVER vanishes/dissolves/warps.

STRUCTURE LAYOUT — STAIRS IMMEDIATELY INSIDE: the modest structure (shed, cabin, hut, bunker, lighthouse base) is essentially a SMALL ENTRANCE LANDING — when you open the front door, the staircase going DOWN to the hidden lower interior is IMMEDIATELY VISIBLE right there. K1 must show this layout: just inside the door, mid-stride, with the staircase going DOWN clearly visible immediately ahead (not at the end of a room, not down a hallway — RIGHT THERE).

THE DESCENT IS ALWAYS A NORMAL STRAIGHT STEP STAIRCASE going DOWN — structurally attached (treads on stringers attached to side walls and floor), never floating, never unsupported. NEVER a ladder, vertical ladder, rungs, spiral staircase, circular staircase, ship's ladder, rope ladder, or trapdoor with a ladder. The traveler only ever descends — NEVER ascends.

INTERIOR CONSISTENCY (scenes 4 and 5) — critical: across K4 and K5 the hidden interior must be PERFECTLY CONSISTENT. Same walls, ceiling, floor, furniture, lighting, palette, and materials in every frame. NO floating elements, NO shape-shifting. The lone traveler in K4 and K5 has IDENTICAL clothing, body, hair/hood, height, gait, and silhouette — he MUST NOT change appearance, melt, morph, or duplicate. He walks in ONE consistent forward direction per clip.
